title: Illustrative v1alpha2 register for the evidence-level rules
description: A fixture. Every claim here is illustrative and none is a claim InferOps makes. The register exists so that each classification rule can be driven over a document that passes it, and then over the same document mutated to break it.

claimStatuses.meaning: An executed record under docs/proof/ supports the statement at the level named, inside the boundary its limitation states.
V1 intends it and nothing has proven it. It may be published only as an intention, and it may cite no evidence record.
Out of V1 scope by an accepted decision. It may not be published as a capability at all, and it may cite no evidence record.

A reader would reasonably expect it and V1 states that it does not have it. It may cite the record that measured the absence, because an absence somebody measured is worth more than one nobody mentions.

evidenceClasses.meaning: A statement in a document. Nothing ran.
A deterministic check over files in this repository. No network, no cluster, no model, no clock, no randomness.
A labelled mock provider that loads no model.
Generated inputs or a simulated environment rather than the real one.
A calculation rather than a measurement.
The real component, on a contributor's own machine, on CPU, with versions and commands recorded.
The real component on authorized cloud CPU capacity, with provider, region, node shape, budget, and verified cleanup recorded.
The real component on authorized cloud GPU capacity, with the accelerator stack, allocation mode, budget window, and verified cleanup recorded.
Operating the thing in an organization's production. Part of the published evidence vocabulary and unreachable from this repository.

areas.name: The inference API and its adapters
Real serving on a contributor's machine

limitations: An illustration of shapes. Nothing in this document was run, and no path it cites is a committed record.

claims.statement: An illustrative claim that a completion is served through the real API, adapter, runtime, and pinned model.

evidenceRecords.summary: A committed schema and its fixtures were validated by a deterministic check that executed no part of the behaviour the claim is about.

executedComponents.note: Reads committed files. No network, no cluster, no model, no clock.

workload.description: No request was issued. The check reads files.

results.statement: Every valid fixture validated and every invalid fixture was refused by the rule the matrix names.

limitations: The schema and its fixtures are files. Nothing consumed the contract at run time.
doesNotEstablish: That any workload was ever deployed from a contract document.

evidenceRecords.summary: The real API and adapter executed against a fake inference provider configured to time out. The provider is material to the claim and was replaced, which is what puts this record at C1.

substitutions.rationale: The claim is about what the API does when the provider times out, so the provider had to be controlled. Replacing it is what the record may not be read past.

results.statement: The API returned the canonical timeout response with a retryable flag.

limitations: The provider was a fake. Making it more faithful would not change what the record establishes.
doesNotEstablish: That the real inference runtime behaves this way under a real timeout.

evidenceRecords.summary: A generated request traversed the real API, the real adapter, the real inference runtime, and the pinned model. The input was synthetic and no component material to the claim was substituted, so the record is C2 and not C1.

substitutions.rationale: Telemetry was captured in-process rather than scraped. Nothing about the completion depends on it, and it is recorded so a reviewer decides that rather than assuming it.

workload.description: One generated prompt of a fixed length, issued once.

measurement.method: One request issued and its response body, status, and wall-clock duration recorded.

results.statement: The pinned model returned a non-empty completion through the real path.

limitations: One request on one contributor's CPU. Nothing about capacity, latency under load, or an accelerator follows.
doesNotEstablish: Representative capacity, a sustained latency target, or behaviour under a production workload distribution.

claims.limitation: An illustrative boundary. The records are shapes, and the claim is not one InferOps makes.
claims.doesNotEstablish: Anything at all about InferOps. It is a fixture.

claims.statement: An illustrative claim that a declared latency and error-rate budget is met under representative load.

evidenceRecords.summary: The real serving path was exercised under a workload constructed to represent expected request size and concurrency, against criteria registered before the run.

workload.description: Generated prompts drawn from a declared length distribution at a declared arrival rate.

shape.promptSizeDistribution: Two hundred to eight hundred tokens, uniform.
shape.arrivalPattern: Poisson at eight requests per second.

representativeness.intendedUse: An interactive assistant serving short prompts at moderate concurrency.
assumptions: Expected prompts fall inside the declared length distribution; longer ones are outside what this run says anything about.
Arrival is independent between callers, which a shared client or a retry storm would break.

environment.note: A single-node CPU cluster standing in for the declared deployment shape; the assumptions above say where that stops holding.

measurement.method: Per-request latency recorded at the caller and summarised over the whole window; errors counted separately from timeouts.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The p95 end-to-end latency stays under the declared budget for the whole window.
The error rate stays under the declared budget for the whole window.

results.statement: Observed p95 latency over the window.
Observed error rate over the window, above the declared budget.

limitations: One workload distribution, one node shape, one five-minute window. A criterion was not met and the record keeps it rather than dropping it.
doesNotEstablish: Behaviour outside the tested distribution, infrastructure, or duration, and nothing about production operation.

claims.limitation: An illustrative boundary. The record measured one distribution on one node shape for five minutes.
claims.doesNotEstablish: Anything at all about InferOps. It is a fixture.
claims.notClaimedReason: The error-rate criterion registered before the run was not met, and the record that measured the failure is kept rather than hidden.

claims.statement: An illustrative claim that a service meets its targets under genuine production traffic.

evidenceRecords.summary: An illustrative shape only. No evidence in this repository is C4 and none can be, because there is no organizational production to draw it from.

workload.description: Whatever the depending workload sent during the window.

commands: An illustrative export of the production dashboard over the window.

measurement.method: Production telemetry aggregated over the observation window.

productionContext.organization: An organization operating the platform for its own users.
productionContext.dependingWorkload: A product feature whose users depended on the service during the window.
knownGaps: No failure of the kind the claim is about occurred during the window, so the window says nothing about it.

limitations: One organization, one window, one workload. A month of operation in which a failure never happened says nothing about that failure.
doesNotEstablish: Future performance, or behaviour under failure modes that did not occur during the window.

claims.limitation: An illustrative boundary. No evidence in this repository is C4 and none can be.
